definitions.explanation: A family unit or household, especially in the context of managing daily life, finances, and domestic affairs. Often carries the nuance of the practical side of running a home.

examples.japanese: {所帯|しょたい}を{持|も}つと{責任|せきにん}が{増|ふ}える。
examples.english: Having a household increases your responsibilities.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}くして{所帯|しょたい}を{持|も}った。
examples.english: He started a family at a young age.

examples.japanese: あの{人|ひと}は{所帯|しょたい}じみた{話|はなし}ばかりするようになった。
examples.english: That person has started talking about nothing but domestic matters.

notes:
USAGE:
{所帯|しょたい}を{持|も}つ is a set phrase meaning to start a household or get married and settle down. The word focuses on the practical, everyday side of family life rather than the emotional bonds.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {所帯|しょたい}を{持|も}つ (to start a household; to settle down)
- {所帯|しょたい}じみた (domestic-looking; frumpy)
- {所帯|しょたい}{持|も}ち (a person with a family to support)
- {大所帯|おおじょたい} (a large group or household)

NOTE ON READING:
The word {大所帯|おおじょたい} uses the voiced reading じょたい rather than しょたい.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {世帯|せたい}: household — more administrative and statistical; used on official forms and in census data
- {家庭|かてい}: home; family — emphasizes the warm, nurturing aspect of home life
